## Interactive Plot
The objective of this section is to visualize a movement signal and its tangential speed using the Plotly library. Plotly creates interactive plots that allow us to inspect the data, zoom in and out, and explore the relationship between position and tangential speed.

We use the time and signal variables generated in Section 1 and the tangential_speed() function implemented in Section 3. The three columns of signal represent the x, y, and z coordinates. We calculate the tangential speed from the existing function and display all four quantities against time. Plotly allows us to inspect the curves interactively using hover information and zoom controls.

```{python}

# Calculate tangential speed using the existing function
speed = tangential_speed(signal, time)

# Create an interactive figure
fig = go.Figure()

# Add the three position components
fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x=time[:, 0],
        y=signal[:, 0],
        mode="lines",
        name="X position"
    )
)

fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x=time[:, 0],
        y=signal[:, 1],
        mode="lines",
        name="Y position"
    )
)

fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x=time[:, 0],
        y=signal[:, 2],
        mode="lines",
        name="Z position"
    )
)

# Add tangential speed
fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x=time[:, 0],
        y=speed,
        mode="lines",
        name="Tangential speed"
    )
)

# Configure the interactive plot
fig.update_layout(
    title="Position Signal and Tangential Speed",
    xaxis_title="Time (s)",
    yaxis_title="Position / Speed",
    hovermode="x unified"
)

fig.show()
```
